questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Recognize a conclusion restated as a premise
questions.stem: Note TR-457 defends a gloss by saying it is clear because it is understandable.

answer.exemplar: The defense restates the claim using a synonym, which proves nothing; the note should give an independent reason the gloss is clear.

questions.explanation: Restating the conclusion with a synonym is still circular. Independent support is needed.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Spot a word shifting meaning mid-argument

stimulus.body: Note TR-458 argues a sentence is bright because it has light, then calls it bright in mood.

questions.stem: In note TR-458, what fallacy is committed?

options.text: The word bright shifts from light to mood.

questions.explanation: The argument trades on two senses of bright. Once the shift is exposed, the inference fails.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify a conclusion that does not follow

stimulus.body: Note TR-459 says the text is short, therefore the translation must be expanded.

questions.stem: Stage 1: What is the core flaw in note TR-459?

options.text: Shortness of source does not imply expansion is needed.

questions.explanation: The source's shortness does not justify expansion. The conclusion is unsupported.
questions.hint: Check the link between length and expansion.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate whether a warrant supports the claim
questions.stem: Stage 1: Note TR-460 assumes a name must be kept because names are untranslatable.

options.text: The warrant that names are untranslatable is false.

questions.explanation: Names often have target-language equivalents. The warrant must be tested, not assumed.
